subject: general
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.**

With one goal remaining, they weren't **__out of the woods__** just yet.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Free from difficulties and dangers.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'out of the woods'** means to be free from difficulties and dangers. (खतरे या कठिनाई से बाहर)

 
 
• **Example:** *We are not **out of the woods**__ but we have been thrown a lifeline.*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the team still had one goal to achieve and hence they were not yet free from difficulties and dangers.
 
• This idiom is often used to describe a situation where someone has overcome a difficult situation or danger.
 
• So, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **'Without hope'** does not fit the context of the sentence as the team still had a chance to achieve their goal. (बिना उम्मीद के)
 
• **'Under his control'** is not relevant to the context of the sentence as it does not describe the team's situation. (नियंत्रण में)
 
• **'Between two dangers' **also does not fit the context of the sentence as there is no mention of multiple dangers. (दो खतरों के बीच)
